scenario.description: A credit committee chair must decide whether to grant a temporary leverage-covenant waiver to an industrial borrower and finalize the waiver terms, borrower cure, monitoring, and legal protections, with input from covenant risk, relationship management, and legal.

shared_context.S1: The industrial borrower has reported leverage of 4.3x against a 4.0x maximum leverage covenant.
shared_context.S2: The borrower has requested temporary relief while completing a plant modernization project.
shared_context.S3: No payment default has been reported, and the existing loan remains current.
shared_context.S4: Maya makes the binding credit decision.
shared_context.S5: The committee's normal pre-decision process is to hear a risk review, the client coverage update, and legal confirmation before setting any waiver terms.

PF1.text: Jonas recalculated the covenant file this morning and confirmed that policy permits a 90-day waiver for a 4.0x-to-4.5x breach only with a 1.0% waiver fee and monthly leverage reporting; the recalculation is not yet attached to the committee pack.

PF2.text: Victor found in the executed credit agreement while reviewing the file this week that any leverage waiver must preserve all cross-default rights and state that it does not establish a course of dealing; his draft waiver language has not yet been circulated.

PF3.text: Elena confirmed with the borrower yesterday that it will make a $500,000 principal prepayment by 2026-08-31, which is the condition the borrower can satisfy to bring the temporary leverage limit to 4.5x; this commitment is recorded in her client notes but not in the loan system.

acceptance_conditions: The waiver must be approved with a temporary leverage limit of exactly 4.5x.
The waiver must last exactly 90 days.
A waiver fee of exactly 1.0% must be charged.
Monthly leverage reporting must be required.
The borrower must commit to a $500,000 principal prepayment due by 2026-08-31.
The waiver must preserve cross-default rights and include no-course-of-dealing language.
The decision must cite the covenant risk review as justification.

decisive_facts.why: The shared facts establish only a 4.3x breach; PF1 changes the waiver duration to exactly 90 days, the fee to exactly 1.0%, and monitoring to monthly reporting.
The shared facts contain no waiver language, while PF2 changes the legal terms by requiring preservation of cross-default rights and no-course-of-dealing language.
The shared facts show a current borrower but no executable cure; PF3 changes the decision to an approved waiver at exactly 4.5x conditioned on a $500,000 prepayment by 2026-08-31.
